title: Code review, version control, reproducible builds and release checks
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify important assumptions and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a reviewed and tested exercise.

understand.concept: A professional release workflow reviews source diffs, checks interfaces and ownership, runs tests and static/runtime diagnostics, records toolchain versions and produces a reproducible build artifact. Version control provides traceability and rollback.
understand.whyItMatters: Release discipline reduces the risk of shipping unreviewed defects and makes failures easier to reproduce after deployment.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.

explain.narrative:
A professional release workflow reviews source diffs, checks interfaces and ownership, runs tests and static/runtime diagnostics, records toolchain versions and produces a reproducible build artifact. Version control provides traceability and rollback.

State assumptions and constraints, consult the applicable standard or tool documentation, and verify the result with appropriate compiler diagnostics and tests. Separate portable guarantees from implementation-specific behaviour.

hints: Review the exact commit that will be released.
